entities.summary: Waitstill Hastings Sharp was an American Unitarian minister who was involved in humanitarian and relief work in Czechoslovakia and southern Europe in 1939 and 1940, just before and during World War II. With his wife, Martha, he provided relief aid to refugees, many of them Jewish, fleeing from Nazi Germany and countries under Nazi control and assisted people in danger of persecution to flee Czechoslovakia and France and resettle in the United States and elsewhere. In 2005, Waitstill and Martha were named by Yad Vashem as Righteous among the Nations, the second and third of five Americans to receive this honor.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Waitstill Sharp's humanitarian work in Czechoslovakia and southern Europe helped save thousands of Jewish refugees from Nazi persecution, with his wife Martha assisting over 1,000 people to flee to safety. This selfless act had a significant regional impact, highlighting the importance of individual action during times of crisis.
